get.summary: Liveness probe
get.description:
Answers 'is this process up', not 'is the whole system healthy'.

Deliberately touches no provider and no database. Conflating the two makes
deploys hard to debug, because a failing dependency looks like a dead process.

get.summary: Follow a run as Server-Sent Events
get.description:
Replay the run's stored events after the last id seen, then follow it live.

The id comes from the `Last-Event-ID` header, which the browser sends when
it reconnects, or else from `?last_event_id=`; the header wins. The stream
ends after `job.finished`, so a finished run replays and closes. It also
ends when the session or the membership does; the browser's reconnect then
gets 401 or 404.

post.summary: Compile a vocabulary into a Boolean query
post.description:
Show exactly what will be searched for, before anything is searched.

Concepts sharing a theme are OR'd; themes are AND'd:

    ("chatbot" OR "conversational agent") AND ("humanitarian" OR "crisis response")

Pure and deterministic — the same vocabulary always produces the same query,
and no model is consulted for either origin. That is what makes a
`user_supplied` vocabulary strict by construction rather than by discipline.

This endpoint exists so a reviewer can inspect and argue about the query
itself, which is the transparency commitment made concrete.

get.summary: Search sources available in this process
get.description:
Which repositories this deployment can currently reach.

One entry today. It becomes the list a reviewer checks to know what a run
did and did not cover — and an empty or unexpected entry here is the first
sign a run is not reproducible.

schema.title: Response Sources Api V1 Sources Get

post.summary: Compile a vocabulary and search for papers
post.description:
Run a vocabulary against the configured source.

The response carries the compiled query and its provenance alongside the
results, because a result set separated from the query that produced it
cannot be audited.

Currently backed by an in-memory corpus. The endpoint, the request body and
the response shape do not change when a real source is wired in — only
`api/dependencies.py` does.

tags.description: Signing in and out. Sessions are server-side, carried in a `__Host-session` cookie; every write also needs the `X-CSRF-Token` header, copied from the `__Host-csrf` cookie.

tags.name: account
tags.description: The signed-in user's own sessions, password and second factors.

tags.name: projects
tags.description: Projects and their members. A project is the unit of access, encryption and deletion: non-members get 404 for everything about it.

tags.name: vocabulary
tags.description: Turning curated terms into a Boolean query. Concepts sharing a theme are OR'd; themes are AND'd. A user-supplied vocabulary is used exactly as given.

tags.name: search
tags.description: Running a compiled query against a source. Results always travel with the query and provenance that produced them.

tags.name: reviews
tags.description: Questions inside a project, encrypted with its key.

tags.name: plans
tags.description: The search-planning conversation of a review: clarifying questions, drafts, change requests, acceptance, your own terms (used exactly as given), versions with their differences, and a receipt of what each model call received.

tags.name: papers
tags.description: A run's papers and screening decisions with their provenance, PRISMA counts and the run manifest. Read-only; text is served masked.

tags.name: runs
tags.description: Background runs of a review's pipeline stages. Start one, follow it as Server-Sent Events (reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID`), decide its gates, cancel it. These paths name a review, run or gate; a non-member gets 404.

tags.name: briefs
tags.description: Reading a decision brief, its cited sources and how it was made. Briefs are written by a run's `answer` stage. A non-member gets 404.

tags.name: exports
tags.description: Downloads of a review's results: the screening dataset, included papers, PRISMA counts, the run manifest and the brief. Audited, never cached.

tags.name: questions
tags.description: Follow-up questions in threads, answered in the background from the review's evidence. The question is masked before it is stored or sent.

tags.name: masking
tags.description: A project's masking rules: terms always masked in every text. Owners only; terms are raw text, sealed at rest, and every listing is audited.

tags.name: documents
tags.description: A project's own files: upload (multipart), scanning, reading and masking in the background, the owner's masking review, and approval before any model sees one.
